turns.text: Which order failed in the order system on 2026-09-14, and why?
turns.answer:
The only failed order on 2026-09-14 was **O-88412**. The order system logged it at 14:02:11 UTC as `ERROR order O-88412 payment declined: card expired`.

I checked all 60,000 event-log lines for that day: 59,999 are `ok` and this is the only error.

The same order also has an earlier `INFO order O-88412 ok` entry at 05:06:52 UTC. The log doesn't explain why an order marked ok in the morning shows a payment decline in the afternoon, so that is worth checking with whoever owns the order system.

turns.text: Look at the suppliers of the 8 SKUs that sold the most units in Q3 2026. For each distinct supplier compare the lead time in the supplier master with the one quoted on the supplier portal. How many of them disagree, which supplier has the largest gap, and how many days is that gap?
turns.answer:
**One supplier disagrees: Tirupur Apparel (SUP-13) has the largest gap, at 7 days.**

The 8 best-selling SKUs by units in Q3 2026 (1 Jul to 30 Sep) come from 8 distinct suppliers. For each, I compared the lead time in the supplier master with the one quoted on the supplier portal:

| Supplier | Master (days) | Portal (days) | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Leeds Textiles (SUP-16) | 32 | 32 | 0 |
| Lyon Mills (SUP-19) | 38 | 38 | 0 |
| Hanoi Mills (SUP-24) | 34 | 34 | 0 |
| Prato Knit Co (SUP-22) | 21 | 21 | 0 |
| Hanoi Mills (SUP-09) | 29 | 29 | 0 |
| Bursa Textiles (SUP-06) | 12 | 12 | 0 |
| Tirupur Apparel (SUP-13) | 36 | 43 | 7 |
| Porto Knit Co (SUP-17) | 38 | 38 | 0 |

- **Disagreements:** 1 of the 8 suppliers. Tirupur Apparel's master says 36 days and its portal says 43.
- **Largest gap:** Tirupur Apparel (SUP-13), 7 days.

Two suppliers share the name "Hanoi Mills" (SUP-24 and SUP-09). They have different IDs and different records, so I counted them as separate suppliers. The master records were last updated 2026-03-02 and the portal quotes on 2026-10-28.

turns.text: Gross profit is revenue minus units x the SKU's unit cost. Compute Q3 2026 gross profit for every category from the sales lines and the catalogue, and give the top 3 categories with their gross profit.
turns.answer:
**Top 3 categories by Q3 2026 gross profit (1 Jul to 30 Sep 2026):**

1. **Footwear: £601,745.67**
2. **Knitwear: £591,060.96**
3. **Activewear: £515,888.11**

Dresses came fourth at £502,545.95. Across all eight categories, total revenue was £6,940,992.09 and total cost £2,870,... (see table below for the per-category figures).

| Category | Units | Revenue (£) | Cost (£) | Gross profit (£) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Footwear | 11,978 | 1,123,571.70 | 521,826.03 | 601,745.67 |
| Knitwear | 9,174 | 1,065,612.34 | 474,551.38 | 591,060.96 |
| Activewear | 7,998 | 924,709.56 | 408,821.45 | 515,888.11 |
| Dresses | 12,814 | 952,282.97 | 449,737.02 | 502,545.95 |
| Denim | 8,514 | 784,850.47 | 370,772.27 | 414,078.20 |
| Shirts | 7,637 | 728,269.05 | 336,091.13 | 392,177.92 |
| Outerwear | 7,316 | 708,357.35 | 337,755.81 | 370,601.54 |
| Accessories | 6,553 | 653,338.65 | 320,395.28 | 332,943.37 |

Gross profit is revenue minus units × the SKU's unit cost. Units and revenue are summed per SKU from the Q3 sales, and the cost uses the unit cost in the current catalogue, not the cost at the time of each sale. Every SKU with Q3 sales matched a catalogue entry, and the category revenue adds up to the Q3 total.
